newsitem.title: USA: Kantor says U.S. exports set for record high.
newsitem.headline: Kantor says U.S. exports set for record high.

text.p: Secretary of Commerce Mickey Kantor said Friday that U.S. exports were set to reach a record high this year after a government report showed exports rising three percent in August.

"Our exports are on track for a new record high, they are clearly going to exceed $800 billion this year and well over $600 billion in the goods category alone," Kantor told reporters following release of a report showing the U.S. trade deficit falling by 6.6 percent in August to $10.83 billion.
Kantor said that despite a sharp rise in the monthly trade gap with China in August, the rate of increase was far slower than it had been.
"Our trade deficit with China is increasing at an ever decreasing rate," Kantor said.

The report showed the trade gap with China shot up 23.4 percent to $4.71 billion in August, only the second time that China has surpassed Japan as the country with the biggest trade surplus with the United States.
He blamed the rise on sanctuary markets that keep U.S. goods out of the Chinese market and said more progress was needed in trimming the gap.

"We are making progress, partly because of trade agreements which we have implemented and partly because of the pressure we have put on China to open up their markets," Kantor said in a telephone conference with reporters.
Kantor said that despite a sharp rise in the monthly trade gap with China in August, the rate of increase was narrowing.
On Japan, Kantor said the U.S. trade position was improving.
"We've dramatically improved our trade picture with Japan," Kantor said.

The report said the deficit with Japan fell in August by 11.8 percent to $3.8 billion. The department said that during the first eight months of 1996, the cumulative deficit with Japan has fallen to $30.36 billion from $42.46 billion in the comparable 1995 period, the lowest since 1992.
